title: Root locus
equipment: Rigid rotary shaft with measured velocity
physicalPurpose: Choose a proportional gain that positions the shaft with limited overshoot and settling error.
objective: Choose Kp from a Control Studio root locus with Kd fixed, then test the actual ST shaft response.

simplifications: Rigid shaft with fixed inertia and viscous friction
Direct measured velocity feedback without a derivative filter
Continuous model predicts poles; ST control updates every 20 ms

baseline.limitation: The slower pole at -2 predicts slower decay than the repeated -4 poles at Kp=16; measured requirements must still be checked.

change.decision: Use the Control Studio locus to select Kp; keep or reject it using matched recorded step responses.

acceptance.window: every sample from 4–8 s after the target step

abortPredicates: Angle leaves ±2 rad or velocity leaves ±10 rad/s
Applied torque leaves ±20 N·m; contact with the limit is recorded saturation
Required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Plant, reset, Kd, timing or limits differ from the reviewed comparison
safety.restorationMode: Disable experiment, confirm zero torque, then restart the simulator to reset angle and velocity.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised motion-controls engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical servo gain application
Physical validation requires independent mechanics, drive, topology, model, limits, interlocks, rollback, and explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Choose Kp from the displayed pole paths and verify the actual shaft response.

learning.context: One simulated shaft uses proportional position control and fixed measured-velocity braking.
learning.reason: A pole calculation describes one gain; we need to see how changing Kp moves the poles.
theory: A root locus plots closed-loop pole locations as one gain changes.
Real parts describe decay or growth; imaginary parts describe oscillation.
For fixed Kd=7, the shaft equation is s²+8s+Kp=0.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate the pole pairs for Kp12,16,20 and predict their decay and oscillation before testing.
practicalPreparation: Confirm shaft J=B=1, Kd=7, 20 ms update and torque ±20 N·m.
Start each trial from zero angle and velocity.
learning.change: Select Kp16 from the locus, giving a repeated pole at -4.
learning.comparison: Change only Kp; keep the plant, Kd, reset and target step fixed.
learning.validation: Peak angle≤1.1 rad and absolute error≤.02 rad throughout4–8s.
learning.explanation: Moving the slower pole left predicts faster decay; sampling and torque saturation still require measured validation.
learning.transfer: Use Routh–Hurwitz next to find the stable integral-gain interval of the cubic.
